stories.summary: At the ASEAN Summit retreat in Manila on 15 Nov, PM Lawrence Wong called for a regional platform to share information on companies behind fires causing transboundary haze, building on the existing Singapore–Indonesia joint taskforce; he also urged restraint over the Thailand–Cambodia border dispute and a clearer roadmap for Myanmar's return.
stories.title: PM Wong calls for regional platform to tackle haze issue
stories.why: It sets the agenda for Singapore's ASEAN chairmanship year in 2027, including the haze and Myanmar files it will inherit.

stories.summary: ASEAN and China have provisionally agreed on about 80% of the long-delayed Code of Conduct in the South China Sea, Philippine Foreign Secretary Lazaro said on 15 Nov, but the code will not be finished during Manila's chairmanship and Singapore will inherit the remaining talks when it takes over in 2027.
stories.title: ASEAN–China South China Sea code nears 80% agreement
stories.why: Singapore takes over the toughest unfinished negotiation in the region when it assumes the chair.

stories.summary: Honeywell and Keppel's infrastructure division announced a collaboration to expand low-carbon fuel production, including sustainable aviation fuel, across Asia-Pacific; SAF is expected to make up 1% of fuel for flights departing Changi in 2026, with the regional market projected to grow from US$1.07 billion to over US$7.6 billion by 2031.
stories.title: Honeywell and Keppel target Asia-Pacific SAF expansion
stories.why: It anchors Singapore's bid to be the region's sustainable aviation fuel hub.

stories.summary: Fourteen hawker centres, including Chinatown Complex, Chong Pang, Kovan-Hougang and Tiong Bahru markets, will close for one to five days between 16 and 23 Nov for regular cleaning, the National Environment Agency said.
stories.title: 14 hawker centres to close for cleaning between Nov 16 and 23
stories.why: A practical heads-up for the week ahead — several of the busiest centres are affected.

stories.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Fox News on 15 Nov that Nvidia's board should recruit its next CEO from outside and give answers within 10 days on whether the company knew its advanced chips were being smuggled to China, including via Singapore-based Megaspeed.
stories.title: Bessent calls for outside CEO at Nvidia, demands probe into China chip smuggling
stories.why: Washington is turning the Huang resignation into a full export-control investigation, with Singapore at the centre of the smuggling route.

stories.summary: Jensen Huang is weighing a comeback days after resigning as Nvidia CEO, with allies including Elon Musk and Epic's Tim Sweeney building a campaign urging the board to reappoint him; Nvidia's board probe into his conduct is ongoing and the company reports earnings on 17 Nov.
stories.title: Jensen Huang comeback under works as allies lobby Nvidia to bring back scandal-plagued ex-CEO
stories.why: The board faces a public pressure campaign days before its first earnings call without Huang.

stories.summary: The UK Employment Appeal Tribunal ruled that litigants using generative AI to prepare court documents must personally check them for accuracy, relevance and procedural compliance, after a claimant's ChatGPT-created skeleton argument reached the tribunal.
stories.title: Litigants must check accuracy of AI-generated documents
stories.why: Courts are now putting personal responsibility for AI-drafted filings squarely on the litigant.

stories.summary: XPeng reports third-quarter earnings on Monday 16 Nov after record deliveries of 118,390 vehicles in Q3, up 15% on the quarter; Wall Street expects a loss of $0.11 per share as heavy spending on AI and its IRON humanoid robots weighs on profitability.
stories.title: XPeng stock down 54% YTD as earnings loom
stories.why: It tests whether record EV sales can offset the cost of the company's AI and robotics bet.

stories.summary: Japan's economy shrank at an annualised 0.1% in the July–September quarter, its first contraction in a year, missing forecasts of 0.3% growth; private consumption fell 0.3% and exports slipped, though business investment rose 1.6%.
stories.title: Japan's Q3 GDP dropped an annualized 0.1%
stories.why: A weak print just weeks before the Bank of Japan's December meeting, where a rate rise to 1.5% is widely expected.

stories.summary: Global equities held up despite the Nvidia turmoil and a global Microsoft outage, while hot US October inflation (CPI +0.4%, core +0.3%) has markets fully pricing a quarter-point Fed hike in December, with the 10-year Treasury yield at 5.14% and the dollar at its highest since April 2025.
stories.title: Fin-X Weekly Update 16th November 2026
stories.why: The week ahead — Nvidia earnings, Fed minutes, US retail sales and a Trump–Xi–Putin meeting — will test whether the AI rally can hold.

stories.summary: Asian markets were set for a mixed open on Monday, with Nikkei 225 and Hang Seng futures pointing higher while Australia's ASX 200 edged lower, as traders awaited China's October data and Japan's GDP figures.
stories.title: Nikkei 225 and Hang Seng set for higher open as traders await economic data
stories.why: China's October data lands later today and will set the tone for Asian markets this week.

stories.summary: The Philippines and Australia signed a Defense Cooperation Arrangement in Manila on 15 Nov, witnessed by PM Anthony Albanese, streamlining joint military activities and disaster response under their status of forces agreement and strengthening Manila's deterrent posture in the West Philippine Sea.
stories.title: PH, Australia sign defense cooperation
stories.why: It hardens a key regional security partnership as South China Sea tensions rise.

stories.summary: The USS Theodore Roosevelt entered US Central Command's area of responsibility on 15 Nov, bringing three US carrier strike groups to the Middle East — alongside the USS George H.W. Bush and USS George Washington — amid tensions with Iran and debate in Washington over resuming large-scale operations.
stories.title: US sends third aircraft carrier to Middle East as Donald Trump heads for China talks
stories.why: Three carriers in the region at once is a concentration of naval power last seen in April, days before Trump meets Xi and Putin to discuss Iran.

stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard said it fired six drones at the US air defence radar at Bahrain's Al-Riffa helicopter base early on 15 Nov, its second strike on a Gulf target in 72 hours; US Central Command said it shot down two drones with no casualties or damage, and Bahrain said its defences intercepted the rest.
stories.title: Iran fires six drones at Al-Riffa radar station in second Gulf attack in three days
stories.why: The claim and the denial leave the damage disputed, but the tempo of attacks on Gulf targets is clearly rising.

stories.summary: Estonia will close all three of its border crossings with Russia from 1 December after eight people were detained over an attempted arson attack on drone maker Threod Systems, which Tallinn says was ordered by Russia's GRU military intelligence.
stories.title: Estonia to close Russian border crossings after attempted arson attack
stories.why: A NATO state is shutting its entire land border with Russia over a sabotage attempt on its defence industry.

stories.summary: OSINT firm Golden Owl documented 164 accounts on X posing as French citizens — some run from Iran, according to X's own location data — that have pushed French protest content for three years and drawn at least 46 million views, with 33 million of those since France's unrest began in September.
stories.title: French by identity, Iranian by infrastructure: inside a network exploiting social unrest
stories.why: It shows how a foreign-run persona network can embed itself in a country's street protests and keep operating through an internet shutdown.

stories.summary: An international investigation led by Japan's JPCERT/CC has identified about 1,000 servers suspected of supporting AI-driven cyberattacks since October, with attackers using AI tools to scan for vulnerabilities and target websites worldwide; 600–700 servers are still being tracked.
stories.title: Japan-led probe finds 1,000 servers suspected of supporting AI-driven cyberattacks
stories.why: AI is now doing the reconnaissance for cyberattacks at industrial scale.

stories.summary: Academics Marc Owen Jones and Sohan D'Souza traced a covert influence campaign targeting Britain back to production in Israel, recording 533 million exposures; Facebook pages such as Save Europe spent over £500,000 on adverts in 2024 warning of an Islamic takeover of Britain.
stories.title: How Israelis spent millions to spread anti-Muslim hate on the internet
stories.why: By recorded reach and ad spend, the researchers call it the biggest covert influence operation targeting the UK yet documented.

tldr: Singapore: PM Wong pushes a regional haze platform at the ASEAN Summit as Singapore prepares to take the chair.
Technology: Bessent demands Nvidia answer within 10 days on chip smuggling as Huang's allies push a comeback.
Finance & global markets: Japan's economy contracts 0.1% in Q3, its first shrinkage in a year.
Defence & military developments: A third US carrier strike group enters the Middle East as Iran fires drones at a US radar site in Bahrain.
Information warfare & Information Operations: 164 Iran-run fake French accounts found exploiting France's unrest, with 46 million views.
